title: Set Up Classic Outlook for Windows
cardText: Set up Microsoft 365, Exchange, IMAP and POP email accounts in classic Outlook for Windows.
Configure mail servers, SMTP authentication and POP message retention.
Let IMAP/Exchange mail synchronise, and safely migrate only missing POP or local archive messages without duplicates.
text: This guide covers classic Outlook for Microsoft 365 and Outlook 2016, 2019, 2021 and 2024.
Choose automatic account setup or manual POP/IMAP configuration according to the provider.
IMAP and Exchange normally restore server-stored folders after account configuration; no PST import is necessary when everything is present.
Check for local-only PST archives, messages, contacts and calendars that do not synchronise with the server.
For POP accounts, preserve locally stored messages and review server retention before moving computers.
When migration is needed, open the original PST separately or copy mail into an isolated Imported Old Mail folder.
Compare messages and check for duplicates before merging, and retain the original backup.

identifySetupType.title: Identify the setup or migration
body: Determine whether this is a new email account or an existing account being moved to another computer.
For an existing account, identify the original email application and account type.
POP messages may exist only on the original computer.
If existing mail is being migrated, protect the original files before configuring the replacement account.

checkExistingAccount.title: Identify the existing account and data
body: On the original computer, open classic Outlook and select File, Account Settings, Account Settings.
On the Email tab, identify whether the account uses POP, IMAP or Exchange.
Open the Data Files tab and identify the files associated with the account.
Check for additional local PST archives containing older messages.
If the original client is not Outlook, identify its mail storage and export format.
Do not remove the old account or uninstall the previous application until local data has been protected.

link.name: Microsoft: Outlook Data Files
link.description: Official information about Outlook PST and OST files.

locateExistingPst.title: Locate the original Outlook PST file
body: Open classic Outlook on the original computer.
Select File, Account Settings, Account Settings, then Data Files.
Identify the PST file associated with the POP account.
Select Open File Location to locate it in Windows.
Check for additional PST files used for archives or other accounts.
Record each required PST filename and location.
Do not assume that the default Outlook Files directory contains every archive.

link.name: Microsoft: Find Outlook Data Files
link.description: Official instructions for locating Outlook PST archives.

link.name: Microsoft: Transfer Outlook Data Files
link.description: Guidance for transferring POP mail data between computers.

locateExistingPst.alt: Classic Outlook Account Settings showing the Data Files tab and Open File Location button
locateExistingPst.caption: Use Account Settings, Data Files and Open File Location to find existing POP mail archives.

investigateMissingPst.title: Locate the original mail before continuing
body: The original mail files have not been located.
Confirm whether the account uses POP, IMAP or Exchange.
Search for additional PST files and check available computer backups.
Check whether Outlook has separate archive data files.
If the original application is different, use its supported backup procedure.
Preserve the original computer and email installation until required mail is recovered.

backupExistingPst.title: Back up the existing POP mailbox
body: Close Outlook completely on the original computer.
Copy the identified PST files to a separate, reliable storage location.
Preserve additional archives and any locally stored contacts or calendars.
Keep an untouched backup throughout the migration.
Do not use a OneDrive-synchronised folder as the working location of an open PST.
Check that the copied files are accessible and have plausible sizes.
Do not delete or modify the original files.

link.name: Microsoft: Export Outlook Mail to PST
link.description: Official backup and export instructions.

protectOriginalMail.title: Protect the original mailbox
body: The original mailbox or local archive has not been backed up.
Preserve the source computer and its Outlook data files.
Identify the relevant POP messages, Sent Items and local archives.
Create and verify a backup before removing accounts or changing data files.
Resume the migration only when the source data is protected.

checkPopServerRetention.title: Check POP message retention
body: On the original computer, open File, Account Settings, Account Settings.
Select the POP account and open Change, More Settings, Advanced where available.
Review Leave a copy of messages on the server.
Check any options that delete server copies after a specified number of days or when deleted locally.
During migration between computers, retaining server copies can help prevent messages disappearing before the replacement account receives them.
Check the provider's mailbox quota before retaining messages indefinitely.
Record the original settings and avoid changing them unnecessarily.

link.name: Microsoft: POP Email on Multiple Computers
link.description: Official explanation of retaining POP mail on the server.

link.name: Microsoft: POP Server Retention Settings
link.description: Help locating the Leave a copy on the server option.

checkExistingCloudMail.title: Check existing IMAP or Exchange mail
body: Open the provider's webmail service where available.
Compare Inbox, Sent Items, Archive and important custom folders with the original Outlook installation.
Check for local-only PST archives, contacts or calendars.
Back up anything that is not available from the server.
Keep the original installation available until the replacement account and any required archives have been verified.

identifyAccountType.title: Identify the email provider and protocol
body: Determine whether the account uses Microsoft 365, Exchange, Outlook.com, Gmail or another mail hosting provider.
Use supported automatic configuration and modern authentication for Microsoft 365 or Exchange.
For manually configured hosting, determine whether IMAP or POP is required.
IMAP synchronises mail and folders across devices.
POP downloads incoming messages and may store them only in a local PST.
Confirm that the provider supports the intended connection type.

link.name: Microsoft: Add an Outlook Email Account
link.description: Official setup instructions for supported email providers.

collectProviderSettings.title: Collect manual email settings
body: Obtain the email address, account username and supported authentication method.
Record the incoming POP or IMAP server hostname.
Record the SMTP server hostname and authentication requirements.
Common IMAP settings use port 993 with SSL/TLS.
Common POP settings use port 995 with SSL/TLS.
Common SMTP submission settings use port 587 with STARTTLS or 465 with SSL/TLS.
Confirm all values against the provider's current documentation.
Check whether OAuth or an app-specific password is required.

link.name: Microsoft: Outlook Account Setup
link.description: Official POP, IMAP and account setup instructions.

link.name: Microsoft: Change Email Server Settings
link.description: Help reviewing incoming and outgoing server configuration.

obtainProviderSettings.title: Obtain the email provider configuration
body: The required mail server or authentication settings are unavailable.
Check the hosting provider's official Outlook configuration instructions.
Confirm the incoming protocol, server names, ports, encryption and authentication.
Check whether POP or IMAP access is enabled for the mailbox.
Do not guess settings or disable TLS to make a connection work.

automaticAccountSetup.title: Add the email account automatically
body: Open classic Outlook and select File, Add Account.
Enter the complete email address and select Connect.
Follow the provider's sign-in procedure.
Complete any required modern authentication or multifactor prompts.
Allow Outlook to detect and configure the account.
Check whether the mailbox appears and starts synchronising.
If automatic configuration fails, investigate whether manual setup is supported.

link.name: Microsoft: Add an Outlook Account
link.description: Official automatic account setup instructions.

checkManualSetupSupported.title: Check manual setup compatibility
body: Identify whether the account belongs to Microsoft 365, Exchange or another provider.
For Microsoft 365, do not substitute POP or IMAP for Exchange connectivity unless the organisation explicitly supports it.
Confirm the hosting provider supports manual POP or IMAP configuration.
Check whether the selected connection type supports the account's authentication requirements.
On managed systems, review any administrator-enforced client access policies.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot Outlook Setup
link.description: Official guidance for unsuccessful Outlook account configuration.

manualAccountSetup.title: Choose manual POP or IMAP setup
body: Open classic Outlook and select File, Add Account.
Enter the email address and expand Advanced options.
Select Let me set up my account manually.
Select Connect.
Choose POP or IMAP according to the required account configuration.
Do not choose POP merely because automatic IMAP setup failed.
Enter the provider's incoming and outgoing server settings when prompted.

link.name: Microsoft: Set Up POP or IMAP in Outlook
link.description: Official manual account configuration instructions.

manualAccountSetup.alt: Classic Outlook Add Account window with Advanced options and manual setup selected
manualAccountSetup.caption: Expand Advanced options and choose Let me set up my account manually.

configureImapAccount.title: Configure IMAP and SMTP
body: Enter the provider's incoming IMAP server hostname.
Configure the specified port and encryption, commonly 993 with SSL/TLS.
Enter the outgoing SMTP server and supported submission port.
Configure SMTP authentication and encryption according to the provider.
Use the required account username and supported sign-in method.
Complete the setup wizard and allow the mailbox to synchronise.
Check the IMAP folder configuration if important folders do not appear.

link.name: Microsoft: Manual Outlook Account Setup
link.description: Official IMAP and SMTP account configuration.

configurePopAccount.title: Configure POP and SMTP
body: Enter the provider's POP incoming server hostname.
Use the required port and encryption, commonly 995 with SSL/TLS.
Enter the outgoing SMTP server, supported port and encryption method.
Enable SMTP authentication where required.
Complete the provider's supported sign-in process.
If an existing PST will be used for delivery, select it only through Outlook's supported data-file configuration.
Never overwrite the original PST or use the only existing copy as an unprotected working file.
Once connected, review the POP message delivery and retention settings.

link.name: Microsoft: Set Up POP in Outlook
link.description: Official POP account setup instructions.

configurePopDelivery.title: Configure POP message delivery
body: Open File, Account Settings, Account Settings.
Select the POP account and open Change, More Settings, Advanced where available.
Review Leave a copy of messages on the server and any automatic removal settings.
During a migration, retaining server copies may prevent the old and new computers from interfering with each other's downloads.
Confirm the PST receiving new POP messages.
Review mailbox storage limits and avoid unintended server deletion.
Test the intended download and retention behaviour.

link.name: Microsoft: POP Email on Multiple Computers
link.description: Official POP server retention and delivery guidance.

troubleshootAccountSetup.title: Investigate mail setup errors
body: Record the exact error displayed by Outlook.
Check the incoming and outgoing server hostnames, ports and encryption.
Confirm POP or IMAP access is enabled by the provider.
Check SMTP authentication, OAuth or app-password requirements.
For managed accounts, verify that Outlook is permitted by organisational policies.
Do not disable encryption or enable insecure legacy authentication as a workaround.
Correct the identified issue and test the connection again.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot Outlook Setup
link.description: Official help for account connection failures.

testAccount.title: Verify sending and receiving
body: Send a plain test message to another accessible email account.
Reply from that account and confirm the response arrives.
Verify the outgoing message appears in the appropriate Sent Items folder.
Check for authentication, Outbox and synchronisation errors.
For POP, confirm new messages reach the intended PST and review server retention.
Once sending and receiving work, identify whether the account is IMAP/Exchange or POP before deciding whether a migration is needed.

checkAccountSyncType.title: Identify whether mail synchronises from the server
body: Check the configured account type in File, Account Settings, Account Settings, Email.
IMAP, Exchange, Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com accounts normally synchronise their server-stored mail and folders.
POP may store downloaded messages and sent mail locally in a PST.
For an IMAP or Exchange account, verify server mail before considering any PST import.
For POP, inspect old local mail and archives for messages that need transferring.

verifyServerSyncedMail.title: Verify IMAP or Exchange folders have synchronised
body: Allow classic Outlook time to synchronise the mailbox, especially on a new computer.
Compare Outlook with the same account in the provider's webmail service where available.
Check Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts, Archive, Deleted Items and custom server folders.
Check older messages and attachments; some folders may be collapsed, filtered or not yet synchronised.
Do not import old PST mail simply because a folder takes time to appear.
If messages are in webmail but missing from Outlook, investigate a synchronisation or folder-visibility issue.
If server-stored mail is correct, check separately for local-only data that webmail cannot restore.

investigateSyncMissing.title: Determine whether missing mail exists on the server
body: Look up a sample of the missing messages in webmail, including Archive and Deleted Items.
If the messages exist on the server, Outlook has a synchronisation, folder visibility, filter or account configuration problem; do not import the old PST.
If the messages are absent from webmail but present on the old computer, check local folders and PST archives.
If messages cannot be found anywhere, preserve the original installation and investigate backups or the email provider.

troubleshootImapSync.title: Resolve missing server messages in Outlook
body: Confirm Outlook is connected to the correct account and folder.
Check view filters, search scope, hidden or unsubscribed IMAP folders and synchronisation status.
Allow Outlook to finish downloading large folders; test again after correcting the identified problem.
Compare with webmail rather than importing local archives to compensate for failed synchronisation.
If server messages still do not appear, record the errors and continue account troubleshooting.

checkMissingMailSource.title: Check whether missing messages are local-only
body: On the original computer, search the old mail application and any separate PST files for the missing messages.
Old POP downloads, local archive folders and PST data may contain messages that are absent from webmail.
If the missing mail is located locally, preserve the source and check the rest of the mailbox for local-only data.
If it cannot be found locally or on the server, importing an unrelated PST will not recover it; investigate original backups or the provider.

checkLocalOnlyData.title: Are there local-only folders or archives?
body: Inspect the original classic Outlook installation after server synchronisation is verified.
Check separately opened PST archives, local-only mail folders, historic POP mail, and messages absent from webmail.
IMAP itself does not synchronise locally stored contacts, calendars or signatures; check whether those require a separate transfer.
If the account's required mail is all present in webmail and there is no local-only data to bring across, no PST import is required.
If required local-only messages exist, back them up and transfer only those messages using the controlled migration path.

confirmLocalBackup.title: Confirm the local mail backup
body: Locate the original PST or other local mail archive on the source computer.
For classic Outlook, use File, Account Settings, Account Settings, Data Files to identify PST archives.
Close Outlook before making a manual PST copy; preserve a separate untouched backup.
For other email applications, use their supported export or backup procedure.
Verify the backup contains old Inbox, Sent Items and local custom folders as required.
Do not begin migration until the original messages are protected.

link.name: Microsoft: Find Outlook Data Files
link.description: Official procedure for locating PST archives.

link.name: Microsoft: Export Outlook Mail to PST
link.description: Official Outlook data export and backup instructions.

checkMigrationRequired.title: Check whether POP or local mail must be transferred
body: For an existing POP setup, check the original PST and any additional local archives.
A newly configured POP account cannot retrieve old messages that were previously removed from the server.
Compare old Inbox, Sent Items and custom folders with messages already visible in the new Outlook account.
Check whether required mail is missing from the destination or whether the old PST can simply be retained as a separate archive.
If no historical mail is needed or everything required is already available, do not perform an import.
If old local mail is required, confirm a verified backup before migrating.

checkMigrationSource.title: Identify the existing mail archive
body: Identify whether the required local-only messages are stored in a PST file or a different email application.
Classic Outlook POP accounts commonly use PST files, but IMAP and Exchange users may also have separate PST archives.
An OST is a synchronisation cache and is not a substitute for a PST backup.
For Thunderbird or Apple Mail, use the source application's supported export procedure.
Preserve a verified source backup and identify the destination account before transferring messages.

link.name: Microsoft: Outlook Data Files
link.description: Official PST and OST information.

checkDestinationMailbox.title: Check the destination mailbox for existing mail
body: Before importing, compare the destination mailbox with the original archive.
Review Inbox, Sent Items, Archive and relevant custom folders.
Check whether older messages already exist in webmail or in another Outlook data file.
Compare sender, recipient, subject, message date and contents for possible overlap.
Check mailbox storage capacity before attempting a large server-backed import.
Do not import the entire archive directly into existing folders when overlap is possible.
Prepare a separate location for reviewing the transferred messages.

prepareStagingFolder.title: Create a separate import staging folder
body: In the destination mailbox, create a folder named Imported Old Mail or a similarly identifiable name.
For IMAP or Exchange, create it beneath the destination account so that copied mail can synchronise to the server.
For a POP-only destination, consider keeping the original PST open as a separate archive instead of copying everything into the active POP data file.
Do not use Inbox, Sent Items or another populated folder for an uncontrolled import.
The staging folder separates imported messages from existing mail; it does not automatically remove duplicates.
If folder creation or the chosen import method is unsuitable, use a separate PST archive until a safe transfer method is available.

chooseMigrationMethod.title: Choose how to transfer existing mail
body: For a PST, the preferred controlled method is to open it separately and copy the required messages into the staging folder.
Classic Outlook also has an Import/Export wizard, but its folder mapping and duplicate options must be reviewed carefully.
For mail stored in another application, use its supported import or export procedure.
Do not run multiple full imports of the same archive without checking what was already transferred.
Choose the method matching the original mail format.

choosePstMigrationMethod.title: Choose PST opening or controlled import
body: Opening a PST makes its messages available in Outlook without merging them into the destination mailbox.
For an old POP mailbox, opening the archive may be sufficient if the user only needs access to historical messages.
For an IMAP or Exchange mailbox, selected old messages can be copied into the separate staging folder.
The Import/Export wizard can also import PST contents, but may map folders into the selected mailbox.
Avoid importing a complete PST directly into Inbox or Sent Items when messages may already exist there.
Use the Import/Export wizard only when the destination and duplicate-handling settings are understood.

link.name: Microsoft: Open Outlook PST
link.description: Official procedure for accessing old mail without importing it.

link.name: Microsoft: PST Import Wizard
link.description: Official classic Outlook PST import procedure.

openExistingPst.title: Open the old PST as a separate archive
body: Copy the old PST to a suitable local folder on the new computer and keep a separate untouched backup.
Open classic Outlook and select File, Open & Export, Open Outlook Data File.
Select the working copy of the PST and open it.
Expand the archive in Outlook's folder pane and check Inbox, Sent Items, custom folders and older messages.
Opening the PST does not merge messages into the active mailbox or change the POP delivery location.
If the user only needs access to historical mail, leaving the PST as a separate archive is sufficient.
Only copy messages to a staging folder if they must be available inside the new mailbox or across devices.

link.name: Microsoft: Open PST in Classic Outlook
link.description: Official instructions for viewing old PST messages.

archiveOrCopy.title: Keep the old PST separate or copy needed messages?
body: Decide whether the old PST is only needed as a readable historical archive.
If a separate archive is sufficient, leave it open in Outlook; there is no need to copy or import its contents into the live mailbox.
If historical mail must synchronise to other devices or appear in current account folders, copy it into the prepared staging folder for review.
Keep a separate untouched backup in either case.

copyPstToStaging.title: Copy old messages into the staging folder
body: Select the messages or folders that need to be present in the destination mailbox.
In the destination account, create or use an Imported Old Mail staging folder; preserve source subfolders under it where practical.
Use Outlook's Copy to Folder command or a supported copy operation to copy selected messages from the old PST.
Do not copy the same archive directly into an existing Inbox or Sent Items folder.
Transfer large archives in manageable batches and track completed batches.
For IMAP or Exchange, allow server upload and verify the messages through webmail.
Before retrying an interrupted copy, inspect the staging folder for items already transferred.
Keep the source PST and its backup unchanged.

link.name: Microsoft: Move or Copy Mail Between Folders
link.description: Official instructions for controlled copying between Outlook folders.

importPstMail.title: Import PST using the classic Outlook wizard
body: Keep an untouched backup of the source PST.
For the safest approach, use Open Outlook Data File and a controlled copy to Imported Old Mail instead of the Import/Export wizard.
If using the wizard, choose File, Open & Export, Import/Export, then Import from another program or file and Outlook Data File (.pst).
Review the choices to replace duplicates, allow duplicates or not import duplicates; Do not import duplicates reduces some overlap but is not guaranteed to find every duplicate.
Select the source folders and Include subfolders where required.
Review Import items into the same folder and Import items into the current folder carefully.
Proceed only if the destination is an intentionally empty, separate folder or data file that keeps imported messages isolated.
If the wizard maps old folders directly into populated Inbox, Sent Items or other existing folders, cancel and use the separate PST plus controlled-copy method.
Allow the import to finish and inspect the actual destination before trying again.
Keep the original PST and check imported messages for overlap before merging.

link.name: Microsoft: Import Outlook PST
link.description: Official instructions covering the Import/Export wizard, destinations and duplicate options.

importPstMail.alt: Classic Outlook Import and Export Wizard showing Import from another program or file
importPstMail.caption: Review the destination and duplicate options carefully. Cancel if the wizard would merge directly into populated folders.

pstRecovery.title: Investigate PST opening or import errors
body: Record the error shown by classic Outlook.
Confirm the file is a complete PST rather than an OST or unsupported mail format.
Check that the copied file is available on a writable local drive.
If PST corruption is suspected, use Microsoft's Inbox Repair tool, SCANPST.EXE, on a working copy.
Keep the untouched original file and backup.
After repair, reopen the PST and verify its messages before transferring data.

link.name: Microsoft: Repair Outlook PST Files
link.description: Official Outlook Inbox Repair tool instructions.

otherClientMigration.title: Transfer mail from another application
body: Identify the source application and original mail storage format.
Use the source client's supported export or import procedure.
Do not rename MBOX or EML files to PST; changing the extension does not convert mail data.
Where supported, import source messages into a compatible client and transfer them into a separate IMAP staging folder.
Keep copies of the original archive and record which folders have been transferred.
Allow server synchronisation to complete before checking the destination in Outlook.
Avoid importing the same messages repeatedly.

checkPartialImport.title: Check incomplete or interrupted transfers
body: Do not immediately repeat the entire PST import or message copy.
Inspect the separate import destination, staging folder or open PST to determine which messages were already transferred.
Compare completed folders, message counts and date ranges with the source.
Check for connection failures, mailbox quota problems and damaged archive items.
Correct the identified problem first.
If another transfer is needed, copy only missing messages or use a clearly labelled new staging folder.
Keep both the partial import and original archive until the result can be reconciled.

reviewStagedMail.title: Review imported mail before merging
body: Compare the separate import destination, staging folder or opened PST with the existing mailbox folders.
Check Inbox, Sent Items, Archive and any custom folders for overlap.
Identify likely duplicates using sender, recipient, subject, date, contents and attachments.
Messages in the same conversation may have identical subjects but still be different messages.
Check that important old POP messages missing from the server are present.
Do not bulk-delete messages solely because subjects or dates match.
Leave uncertain messages separate until they can be checked.
If the staged messages have been reviewed, decide whether to keep them as an archive or merge selected items.

resolveImportDuplicates.title: Resolve duplicate or missing messages
body: Check suspected duplicates against messages already present in the destination.
Compare message contents and attachments rather than relying only on subject lines.
Remove confirmed redundant copies from the staging area only when the required originals exist elsewhere.
Check whether missing messages remain in another PST folder or were excluded from an import.
Process large archives in smaller groups.
Preserve the untouched source backup throughout.
If the results remain uncertain, avoid merging the folders.

chooseMailDestination.title: Keep the archive separate or merge reviewed mail
body: Decide whether the old mail should remain accessible as a separate PST or staging folder.
A separate historical archive may be sufficient for an existing POP account.
If messages need to appear in the normal mailbox folders, transfer only those confirmed to be missing.
Prefer copying reviewed messages before deleting any staged copies.
Do not merge a complete archive into a populated Inbox or Sent Items folder without checking for duplicates.
Keep the original PST backup regardless of the chosen method.

mergeReviewedMail.title: Merge only messages missing from the mailbox
body: Identify the required messages that do not already exist in the destination folders.
Copy them from the staging folder or opened PST into the appropriate Inbox, Sent Items, Archive or custom folders.
Transfer in manageable batches and check each completed batch.
For IMAP or Exchange, allow Outlook to finish uploading the messages.
Verify server-side copies through webmail where available.
Do not remove staging folders or original source files until the result has been confirmed.
If duplicates or missing messages appear, return to the reconciliation step.

link.name: Microsoft: Copy Messages Between Folders
link.description: Official procedures for copying or moving Outlook messages.

verifyMigratedMail.title: Verify old mail and folder structure
body: Compare the destination mailbox or separate PST with the original backup.
Check Inbox, Sent Items, Archive, staging folders and important custom folders.
Verify a selection of older messages and their attachments.
Check for missing or duplicated messages after any merge.
For IMAP or Exchange, confirm that server-bound messages are present in webmail.
For POP, confirm the historical PST remains accessible and new messages reach the intended data file.
Check contacts and calendars separately when required.
Keep the original PST and migration backup until the result has been verified.

migrationEscalation.title: Further Outlook migration required
body: The old messages could not be transferred or reconciled safely.
Preserve the original PST files and any partially imported mail.
Record the source account, destination account, method used and errors encountered.
Check for PST damage, incomplete transfers, insufficient mailbox storage or repeated imports.
Do not merge uncertain message sets or delete source files.
Investigate a supported Outlook repair or controlled migration method before attempting again.

link.name: Microsoft: Repair Outlook PST
link.description: Official Outlook data-file repair instructions.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot PST Import
link.description: Official guidance for Outlook import problems.

setupComplete.title: Classic Outlook setup completed
body: The account sends and receives messages using the intended provider settings.
For IMAP or Exchange, server-stored Inbox, Sent Items, Archive and custom folders have synchronised and been compared with webmail.
If no local-only mail is missing, no PST import was required.
For POP, the data-file location and server retention settings have been reviewed.
Any required local or POP mail is available in a separate verified archive or has been transferred through a staging folder.
Imported messages have been reviewed for duplicates before any merge.
Check local contacts, calendars, signatures and additional archives separately where needed.
Retain verified backups of the original local mail data.

setupEscalation.title: Further classic Outlook setup diagnostics
body: Classic Outlook cannot connect after checking the provider's account settings.
Record the Outlook version, email provider, protocol and exact error message.
Confirm that the provider supports the required authentication method.
For managed accounts, check organisational security and client access policies.
Use the Email Not Working guide for deeper delivery and authentication troubleshooting.
Preserve any existing PST or POP mail data while investigating.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot Outlook Setup
link.description: Official account setup troubleshooting instructions.
